tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist today to set operating/repair disposition; correct per findings, verify vibration against approved limits and trend daily. Obtain source-required attention today. Check latest NDE spectrum, cause and limits.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Strong continuing progression and a growing 1x component support the 7–8 band for loss of gas export compression. Remaining below alarm limits the assessment; neither imminent loss nor an already failed compression function is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the main gas export compressor has a severe operational consequence: platform recycle and production reduction within an hour, with no spare or workaround. This supports 7–8, not an invented extreme accident consequence.

tickets.summary: PSV-1310 tailpipe hiss and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure suggest passing and protection impairment; loss of its nonredundant relief function could expose V-1201 to overpressure. Restoration is unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer: diagnose suspected passing; set operating/repair disposition within regulatory limits and repair if confirmed. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. After repair, test set pressure and tightness. Check gas levels and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is PSV-1310 overpressure protection for V-1201. Audible hissing and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure suggest active passing, an advanced precursor under the supplied guidance. They do not establish inability to relieve overpressure.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure would remove the stated, nonredundant overpressure protection for the first-stage production separator, creating credible major-accident exposure through pressure-boundary failure. Actual release magnitude and personnel exposure are unknown; an extreme consequence is not established.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed first start, then started on attempt 2 after ~8 s and achieved rated pressure; batteries were 22.8 V at rest. Delayed firewater availability matters because partner A's delivery capacity is unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Mechanical engineer to direct repairs per findings and operating disposition; retain weekly tests. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test batteries, charger and starting air. Retest first-start and rated pressure. Verify A flow/pressure versus required duty.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Starting on demand is the assessed function. The 3 June test demonstrated first-attempt failure. Successful starting on the second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking, followed by normal running at rated discharge pressure, does not erase that failure or establish reliable restoration. Battery voltage was measured at rest, not during cranking; the cause remains unconfirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start delays firewater availability and creates severe fire-protection exposure. Full redundancy cannot be credited: on 17 June, linked partner A started correctly but delivered 9.2 barg against 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured. This does not prove A unavailable or establish a combined capacity shortfall. Both pumps being unavailable would require production shutdown; that condition is not established.

tickets.summary: PL-1002 window 2 near the low-point drain measures 6.2 mm versus 7.4 mm minimum under wet insulation; adjacent windows pass, but containment loss could release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to assess operating/repair disposition; implement approved repair, stop water ingress and verify wall >=7.4 mm and pressure integrity. Map CUI; check leaks and repair status. Check personnel exposure and release controls.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pressure containment by PL-1002. Heavy scaling and saturated insulation accompany wall thickness below the supplied minimum, supporting advanced damage. Adjacent windows remain within tolerance. Neither imminent rupture nor actual containment loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this production flowline's containment could release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure, creating severe personnel and major-accident exposure. No redundant line is recorded. Release magnitude, personnel exposure and effective mitigation are unknown, so an extreme consequence is not asserted.

tickets.summary: FG-0455 failed to detect 50% LEL gas with two cylinders; the other two heads responded, retaining compression-module gas detection but losing the 2oo3 group's failure margin.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer to diagnose nonresponse and approve repair/replacement and operating disposition. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Verify current protection control alignment. Retest head at 50% LEL and voted response.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is this individual head's hydrocarbon-gas detection response. No response on the first test or repeat with a second cylinder confirms function loss, despite clean-looking optics. Responding companion heads moderate impact, not this head's likelihood.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure removes one compression-module hydrocarbon-detection channel. Both companion heads responded correctly, supporting moderate protection degradation with remaining capability, not total detection defeat. The voted group loses its additional-failure margin.

tickets.summary: CR-5001 hoist rope has 6 broken wires/lay versus 10 discard in the maximum-radius drum-spooling section, with poor lubrication; hook, sheaves and structure are sound. Failure risks dropped loads and offload loss causing logistics problems within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Lifting engineer/surveyor: inspect full rope/drum path, restore lubrication, set lifting-standard disposition and reinspection; verify below 10 wires/lay and retest hoist. Establish rope break trend and duty. Check lift loads and personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is safe load hoisting by the main hoist rope. Six broken wires per lay remain below the discard criterion of ten, supporting limited degradation with margin. Poor lubrication warrants correction, but the single observation establishes neither strong progression nor operational function loss.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the load-hoisting rope presents a credible dropped-load injury hazard. There is no redundant crane, and loss of supply-boat offloads creates logistics problems within days. This supports a broad severe-consequence band, without assuming fatalities or known personnel exposure.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this nonredundant pump does not stop production immediately, but inhibitor starvation allows downstream carbon steel corrosion within weeks, supporting severe delayed-integrity consequences. Actual downstream damage or personnel exposure is not established.

This does not establish tested separation capacity.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the same liquid-removal function could admit a liquid slug to a turbine, supporting material equipment and operational consequences. No redundant scrubber is listed. Extreme consequences or total installation loss are not established; the score is not based on cleaning cost.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is FW-8101's delivery of required firewater pressure and flow. This does not establish present unavailability or restoration. Both pumps being unavailable would require production shutdown, but that combined condition is not established. The credible major-accident exposure supports a severe, not demonstrated extreme, consequence band.

tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer to approve operating disposition and repair per findings. Check impairment/deviation record. Inspect line/sensor; prove response to approved tolerance. Verify duty control/alarm and safeguards. Review exposure during 36-hour signal loss.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is responsive backup interface-level measurement on V-1201. An unchanged value for approximately 36 hours, explicitly judged incredible for this service, establishes loss of that function despite the unresolved cause. This is not a claim that both channels have failed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of backup measurement materially weakens interface-level control assurance. On June 11, the duty leg read approximately 12 percent above the backup and 15 percent above the sight glass while controlling the process; it also feeds the high-level alarm. The June 18 backup flatline therefore cannot be moderated by assumed healthy duplication. Material operational and potential alarm-protection degradation are supported, but total control loss or a specific major-accident outcome is not established.

tickets.summary: Loose, wind-flapping cladding on K-3401's second-stage discharge line threatens to fall and injure personnel; the finding explicitly identifies no process concern.
tickets.recommended_action: Control access below; inspect adjacent fixings. Have the maintenance engineer approve repair scope; refit loose lagging and cladding and verify secure retention after repair. Inspect cladding and drop-zone exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is retention of the discharge-line lagging and cladding, not gas compression. Loose cladding actively flapping in wind supports advanced degradation and high likelihood of detachment, without establishing imminent or completed detachment. The earlier bearing-vibration finding is a separate mechanism and is not transferred.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of cladding retention creates the explicitly identified dropped-object hazard, with credible serious personnel injury. This supports a broad severe-consequence band, not an extreme consequence claim. Height, mass and personnel access remain unknown. No process concern is explicitly stated, so compressor-trip and production-loss consequences are not attributed to this defect.

tickets.summary: DEL-8300’s north branch isolation defeated wellhead fire-deluge coverage for an unknown duration without logging; the valve was reopened, but restored protection remains unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire protection engineer to inspect valve, restore status tag and approve disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Trace isolation cause, duration and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivering deluge water through the north-quadrant branch. Chained-closed isolation confirmed loss of this function at discovery. Immediate reopening is confirmed, but does not demonstrate restored delivery.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of north-quadrant deluge delivery removes local fire protection above two producing wellheads, creating credible major-accident escalation and personnel exposure. No redundant arrangement is listed. This supports severe exposure, not an asserted total-installation loss or quantified casualty outcome.

tickets.summary: Wet insulation and rust staining at V-1201's manway suggest hidden corrosion threatening first-stage pressure containment; wall condition is unmeasured, so containment loss is not established.
tickets.recommended_action: Obtain integrity engineer operating/repair disposition; repair to findings, renew wet insulation and verify accepted wall/leak integrity. Check containment impairment/deviation status. Strip locally; inspect and UT-map wall. Check pressure, inventory and nearby exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is first-stage pressure containment. Damp insulation and rust staining are meaningful precursors to concealed corrosion, supporting the active-degradation/precursor band. Wall loss, remaining margin and progression are unmeasured; historical thick walls do not establish current margin. Linked piping and instrument defects are not vessel-shell defects.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the entire first-stage production pressure boundary presents credible severe hydrocarbon-release, personnel and operational consequences, with no redundant vessel identified. This supports the severe band, not an extreme scenario without inventory and exposure evidence. Earlier linked PSV, flowline and transmitter findings do not establish this shell's condition or verified effective protection.
